WA-2025-SB6225.title: Authorizing bonds for transportation funding.
WA-2025-SB6225.summary:
General Bond Authorization. Bonding up to $800 million is authorized for the design, right-of-way, and construction of highway projects or improvements, with all proceeds from the sale of any such bonds to be deposited in the Move Ahead Washington Account, which resides in the motor vehicle fund. The bonds are authorized as general obligation bonds of the state. The bonds must be paid first from excise taxes on fuel and vehicle related fees and are secondly backed by the full faith and credit of the state. The Legislature agrees to continue to impose these excise taxes on fuel and vehicle-related fees in amounts sufficient to pay bonds costs.

No bonds may be offered for sale without prior legislative appropriation of the net proceeds of the sale of the bonds. The state treasurer is authorized to transfer amounts needed to the Highway Bond Retirement Account to pay debt service.

State Route 520 Bond Authorization Increase. Existing State Route 520 bond authorization is increased by $500 million, from $1.95 billion to $2.45 billion.

Expiring Unused Bond Authorizations. The authority of the state finance committee to issue remaining unissued bonds expires June 30, 2026 for the following authorizations:

Use Enacted Unissued
WSDOT District 1 HQ 1990 $1.6 million
State match for 1991 federal funds bill, advanced construction, local loans. 1993 $75.2 million
Public private initiatives in chapter 47.46 1994 $6.2 million

WA-2025-SB6137.summary:
Permitting Sports Wagering on College Sports with Limitations. Wagering on a collegiate sport or athletic event that involves a post-secondary educational institution located within Washington is permitted. Wagers on the performance or nonperformance of an individual athlete that is enrolled in a post-secondary educational institution that is located within Washington are prohibited.

A tribe's class III gaming compact may be amended pursuant to the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act to authorize the tribe to conduct and operate sports wagering on any Indian lands. For gambling information transmitted over the internet, a wager may be placed and accepted at a tribe's gaming facility if the customer placing the wager is physically present on the premises of any tribe's gaming facility.

WA-2025-HB2105.title: Concerning immigrant worker protections.
WA-2025-HB2105.summary:
Notices .

Receipt of a Notice of Inspection. Beginning October 1, 2026, an employer must post and distribute notices to its workers and their representatives within five days of receiving an NOI of Forms I-9 and any related worker records from a federal agency, which includes the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Department of Justice Immigrant and Employee Rights Section, the United States Department of Labor, and any other agency enforcing civil immigration laws or employment eligibility requirements.

The notice must include certain information in English and the five most commonly used non-English languages in the state, such as the name of the federal agency, the date of the NOI, the types of records sought, and contact information for a statewide organization that provides advocacy related to immigrant and refugee rights. The notice must also include a copy of the NOI. While an employer may use its own notice, the Attorney General (AG) must develop and publish a model notice for employers to use without requiring translation services, subject to certain requirements in the bill. The model notice must be published by September 1, 2026. An employer that uses the model notice is considered to have satisfied the required elements.

The notice of the NOI must be posted in conspicuous places on the premises of the employer where notices to workers are customarily posted. The employer must also transmit the notice directly to workers using the primary method of communication typically used by the employer, which must include at least one of the following: hand delivery to the worker; mail with proof of delivery; email with proof of transmission; or text message sent telephonically, which may include a link to a notice maintained on a web page, with proof of transmission.

Inspection Results. Beginning October 1, 2026, an employer must distribute notices to affected workers and their representatives within five days of receiving the results of any inspection of Forms I-9 and any related worker records. This applies to any worker identified by the federal agency as lacking federal work authorization or any worker whose Form I-9 has been identified as having deficiencies. The notice must include a copy of the written notice from the federal agency, as well as the following information in the language most regularly used to communicate between the employer and the affected worker:
• a description of any deficiencies or other items identified in the results notice related to the affected worker;
• the time period for correcting any potential deficiencies;
• a mutually agreed upon time and date, or options for times and dates, for a meeting with the employer to correct any identified deficiencies; and
• notice that the worker has the right to representation during any meeting scheduled with the employer.

The notice must be transmitted directly to the affected workers using the primary method of communication typically used…

WA-2025-SB6027.title: Modifying requirements and allowed uses for certain funding related to providing and maintaining affordable housing and related services.
WA-2025-SB6027.summary:
Local Sales and Use Tax for Housing and Related Services. Authorization is added for at least 60 percent of the money to be used for funding the operation and maintenance of existing units of affordable housing and facilities where housing-related programs are provided and rehabilitating existing affordable housing, which may include emergency, transitional, and supportive housing.

For the remainder of the funds, authorization is added for:
• affordable and supportive housing operation and maintenance; or
• rental assistance.

A county or city may enter into an interlocal agreement with one or more counties, cities, or public housing authorities to pool the tax receipts, pledge those taxes to bond issued by one or more parties to the agreement, or allocate the proceeds of the taxes or bonds in accordance with such interlocal agreement and statutory requirements.

Local Mental Health and Chemical Dependency Sales and Use Tax. A county that imposes the tax after a city in that county has imposed the tax must consult, rather than enter into an interlocal agreement, with that city to determine how the services will be allocated and funded in the city.

Local Sales and Use Tax for Affordable and Supportive Housing. Authorization is added for the money to be used for funding the operation and maintenance of existing units of affordable or supportive housing.

Affordable Housing for All Account. The requirements for the 90 percent portion of the funding in the affordable housing for all account are amended to clarify that housing projects must be affordable to extremely low-income households with incomes at or below 30 percent of the area median income at the time of move-in and remove language that the project require a supplement to rent income to cover ongoing expenses.

Eligible uses are added for grant funds to support the building, operations, maintenance and supportive service costs for permanent supportive housing projects or units within those projects that have or will receive funding from the Housing Trust Fund or other public capital funding programs to include:
• resident services, such as programming, community events, and building activities;
• essential ancillary services necessary to assist program participants who are not covered or are partially covered by Medicaid or other health insurance obtain and maintain housing;
• resident needs for basic living and well-being;
• essential maintenance and upkeep; and
• essential case management and other resources with demonstrable connection to resident well-being and housing stability.

When awarding grants Commerce:
• may not impose a cap on administrative or overhead costs for grantees of less than 15 percent of the grant award;
• shall seek to promote continuity of operations and stability for existing projects; and
• must require grantees maintain supporting documentation for all expenses above $50—Commerce may not require the submission of supporting documentation before approving…

WA-2025-HB2325.title: Establishing a tourism self-supported assessment program to fund statewide tourism promotion.
WA-2025-HB2325.summary:
Tourism Assessment Program .

The Authority is authorized to establish a Tourism Assessment Program (TAP), subject to review by the Director of Commerce, that is designed, proposed, and governed by a Ratepayer Oversight Board (ROB). The Authority is required to levy and collect a percentage of a business's gross revenue as an annual assessment. The assessments must be collected on an annual basis, after ratification by the businesses in each industry sector.

The membership of the Authority's Board is modified by expanding the number of members from 13 to 17, and modifying the non-legislative membership as follows:
• eight members nominated by the ROB representing businesses paying the assessments;
• two members representing official state destination marketing organizations;
• two members representing tourism businesses subject to the assessment; and
• one member representing a trade association that represents businesses subject to the assessment.

The Authority, with the review of the Director of Commerce, is required to approve an annual budget for the TAP. The Authority is required to approve or reject the budget recommended by the ROB and may not amend, replace, or independently adopt policies or provisions not submitted by the ROB. The budget must include:
• a complete and detailed financial program of the ROB, showing its revenues and expenditures;
• an explanation describing the administration and implementation of the ROB's programs and priorities and identifying reasons for changes from prior expenditures or revenue items;
• an explanation of changes to financial policies, including an outline of the proposed policies for the ensuing fiscal period and performance indicators that demonstrate measurable progress toward the ROB's priorities; and
• sufficient detail to provide transparency for the ROB's actions on behalf of the tourism industry.

The State Auditor is required to conduct a regular audit of the budget.

The Authority is required to submit an annual report to the Legislature and the Governor.

The Authority is required to adopt rules and give substantial weight to the recommendations in the October 31, 2025, report titled Tourism Self-Supported Assessment Advisory Group: Report to the Legislature and the ROB's proposal. The rules do not apply to federally recognized Indian tribes, businesses, or enterprises unless the tribe or tribal member has opted to participate in the TAP.

The state and its agents are immune from liability for obligations incurred by the Authority or the ROB. Liabilities and claims against the Authority or the ROB are only enforceable against the assets of the Authority or the ROB as if it were a corporation. The liability of the members of the Authority and the ROB are several, not joint, and no member shall be liable for the default of any other member.

WA-2025-HB1500.title: Concerning resale certificates for units in common interest communities.
WA-2025-HB1500.summary:
The resale certificate requirements for units in a CIC subject to the WUCIOA are modified.

Required Contents of a Resale Certificate .

In addition to all the other information that must be included in a resale certificate, the resale certificate must contain:
• the most recent financial audit report available, instead of the audit report for the year immediately preceding the current year;
• all policies, procedures, and resolutions approved by the board that are currently in effect; and
• the most current reserve study for the association, instead of a summary of the current reserve study.

The resale certificate must include the statement "NONE" or "RECORDS UNAVAILABLE" for each category of records that is not provided in the certificate.

Charges for Preparation of a Resale Certificate.

In addition to not exceeding $275, a reasonable charge to the unit owner for preparation of a resale certificate must cover the direct out-of-pocket cost of copying and providing the required information, and may not include any additional charges for providing documents that are maintained in electronic form on a website, web portal, or application available to unit owners. However, an association may charge an additional $100 for a rush service that must be completed within 72 hours of a request. An association may also still charge a nominal fee, not to exceed $100, for updating a resale certificate within six months of the unit owner's previous resale certificate request.

An association may not require a unit owner to contract or establish an account with a third party to provide payment or accept delivery of a resale certificate.

Limitations on Liability.

In addition to the existing limitations on liability, a purchaser is not liable for any violation of the governing documents created by an alteration to a unit that, with reasonable diligence, should have been known to the association or its authorized agent at the time of conveyance but was not identified in the resale certificate.

Cause of Action to Enforce Resale Certificate Requirements.

A unit owner may bring an action to enforce the resale certificate requirements related to fees, timeliness of delivery, accuracy, and completeness. In such an action, the court must award reasonable attorneys' fees and costs and actual damages to any prevailing unit owner. The court may also impose a civil penalty against the association or its authorized agent. An authorized agent that charges a fee for furnishing a resale certificate assumes all liability for the fees charged, and for the timeliness of delivery, accuracy, and completeness of the resale certificate.

WA-2025-HB2523.title: Concerning the community reinvestment program.
WA-2025-HB2523.summary:
The Washington State Office of Equity (Equity), Commerce, and "by and for community organizations," must update the Community Reinvestment Plan (Plan) as needed, but at least every five years, beginning in 2032. The Plan must be developed using a community-based participatory action research approach, and include funding recommendations, programmatic guidelines, funding distribution, long-term economic benefits, monitoring, and evaluation.

At least 15 percent, and no more than 60 percent of the funds must be distributed to each of the following five strategies: economic development, civil and criminal legal assistance, community-based violence intervention and prevention services, reentry services, and agricultural and economic support. The distribution may be modified if Equity, Commerce, and the Plan recommend an alternative allocation to avoid unexpended funds or to avoid limiting access. Certain organizations are eligible for grants statewide, provided that specified criteria are met. The criteria include a limited number of organizations providing services, submission of annual reports, and obtaining a letter of support. Commerce must prohibit organizations that receive a grant from distributing the funds to an officer, family member of an officer, or a business or nonprofit owned or managed by an officer.

A Community Reinvestment Program Work Group (Work Group) is created to prepare a report, legislative recommendations, and a transition plan for joint administration of the Community Reinvestment Program by Equity and Commerce by July 1, 2027, including guidance for an administrative framework. The Work Group must include legislative members, Equity, Commerce, and up to six optional members, and must be chaired by the Equity member. The report must be submitted to the Legislature, including the legislative caucus representing a minority community, by November 1, 2026. Commerce is required to use existing appropriations to fund the Work Group and Equity's participation in the Work Group.

The Washington State Institute for Public Policy is required to study Commerce's distribution of, regional impact of, and the recipient organizations' use of, the funds allocated under the Plan by June 30, 2027. Commerce is required to use existing appropriations to fund the preparation of the report.

WA-2025-HB2248.title: Concerning corporate filings and other documents processed by the secretary of state's corporations and charities division.
WA-2025-HB2248.summary:
Uniform Business Organization Code .

Entity Filings: The SOS must document the date of receipt of an entity filing, rather than "record" the filing. References to "filing" an entity filing are changed to "processing" an entity filing.

Nonprofit corporations and limited liability partnerships formed under Washington law must file an initial report within 120 days of their formation. Fifty dollars of an entity's annual license fee must be deposited with the State Treasurer and the remainder of the fee must be deposited in the SOS's Revolving Fund.

Foreign Entities: A registered foreign entity that changes its name must include a copy of the name change document filed in the entity's home jurisdiction when it files an amendment to its foreign registration statement. Employing a remote worker who resides in Washington is added to the list of activities of a foreign entity that do not constitute doing business in the state.

Trademark Registration .

The requirement that the SOS issue a new certificate in the name of a trademark assignee upon payment of a $5 fee is removed.

International Student Exchange Visitor Placement Organizations .

The SOS must establish procedures for reinstatement of an international student exchange visitor placement organization's terminated registration.

Authentication Services .

The SOS may not certify or attest to the signature of a notary public on an individually created document that can or should be issued as a certified copy from a city, county, or state entity.
WA-2025-HB2248.summarySource: Washington Legislature final bill report (2248-S HBR FBR 26, 2026-04-15)

WA-2025-SB5994.title: Preserving timber tax distributions for school districts with recent school district levy failures.
WA-2025-SB5994.summary:
This bill extends timber tax distributions to school districts without qualifying levies in a given calendar year, if they had qualifying levies in effect in either of the previous two calendar years. The highest levy rate in effect during the two previous calendar years must be used to calculate timber tax distributions.

This bill contains an emergency clause and takes effect immediately.

WA-2025-HB2479.title: Concerning the recovery of unpaid wages.
WA-2025-HB2479.summary:
Wage Recovery Account and Deposits. The Wage Recovery Account (account) is created to be administered by L&I. All civil penalties paid under wage complaints and under the MWA must be deposited in the account. Various statutes under the MWA are amended to deposit civil penalties into the account, rather than the Supplemental Pension Fund.

Wage Recovery Program. The Wage Recovery Program (program) is created to be administered by L&I. The program will allow L&I to disburse funds to unpaid low-wage employees, prior to L&I issuing collecting unpaid wages and interest from an employer, if the employee would experience immediate economic harm due to the nonpayment of wages.

Beginning July 1, 2028, or when the account contains at least $130,000, whichever is later, an employee is eligible to recover from the program if the employee:
• has filed a wage complaint with L&I and L&I has investigated and determined that the wage complaint has merit;
• has assigned the employee's wage complaint to L&I;
• requested to be considered a recipient of funds from the program;
• earnings during the preceding 12 months were less than the maximum amount established by L&I rule;
• attests that without relief from the wage recovery program, the employee will suffer immediate economic harm; and
• has waived the ability to appeal the citation and any notice of assessment and any private right of action.

L&I should attempt to disburse funds after it has determined the complaint has merit and at the earliest possible point in the investigation process. In determining an eligible employee's need for funds, L&I may identify other factors for consideration, such as resources available to the employee, the employee's current employment status, and family size.

L&I may determine the priority of payments made between eligible employees and whether to issue funds for eligible employees. Factors to consider should include, but are not limited to, the severity of the potential economic harm to the employee, whether L&I is likely to recover the unpaid wages and interest from the employer, and availability of funds to be distributed throughout the year given the seasonality of some industries.

An employee receiving funds from the program may not pursue collection, or authorize another entity other than L&I to pursue collection.

Wages and interest paid by an employer to L&I for a wage complaint assigned to L&I must be deposited into the account as necessary to reimburse for the disbursements made to the employee, plus interest. L&I must pay any remaining payment on the claim to the employee.

An eligible employee may receive up to 85 percent of wages the employee is anticipated to be owed, up to a maximum of $2,500. Total payments made under the program for any fiscal year may not be greater than 80 percent of the account balance, calculated at the end of the previous fiscal year.

WA-2025-SB6313.title: Creating the capitol centennial stewardship account and authorizing members of the legislature and statewide elected officials to solicit gifts, grants, and donations to the account.
WA-2025-SB6313.summary:
The Capitol Centennial Stewardship Account is created. Statewide elected officials, including members of the Legislature, may solicit gifts, grants, or donations to the account. Money from the account may only be spent after appropriation, for the following purposes:
• remodeling and repairs to the state capitol public and historic facilities;
• interpretive and educational activities; and
• improvements and activities to enhance public participation in state government.

When soliciting gifts, grants, or donations to the account, statewide elected officials and members of the Legislature are presumed not to be in violation of the solicitation and receipt of gift provisions of the Ethics Act. The Capitol Centennial Stewardship Account and the exemption to the Ethics Act for solicitation of gifts, grants, and donations expire on June 30th, 2033. Any funds remaining in the account on July 1st, 2033, will be transferred to the Capitol Furnishings Preservation Committee Account.
WA-2025-SB6313.summarySource: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (6313 SBR SGTE TA 26, 2026-02-02)

WA-2025-SB6258.title: Creating a nondisciplinary pathway for relinquishing licenses issued by the Washington medical commission.
WA-2025-SB6258.summary:
The commission is authorized to conduct rulemaking for all licenses issued by the commission to allow for the voluntary relinquishment of the license. This includes licenses for MDs, PAs, and CAAs as well as licenses issued under the interstate medical licensure compact and the physician assistant licensure compact.

Under these relinquishment rules, the license cannot be relinquished in lieu of discipline or if the licensee is subject to discipline or under investigation by the commission. The relinquishment is not an adverse action and as such is not reportable to any disciplinary database, the national practitioner data bank, or other websites.

Licensees who request this relinquishment process agree to the permanent relinquishment of the property right and shall have no right to reinstatement or renewal.
WA-2025-SB6258.summarySource: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (6258 SBR HLTC OC 26, 2026-01-30)
